text.title: Rails 7+ Backend Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules grounding the production-grade Rails 7+ methodology — 6 on the service / job architecture, then 4 framework fundamentals on the conventions the app is built out of. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Exactly one `ServiceResult` class MUST exist at `app/services/service_result.rb`. Public API: `success?`, `failure?`, `value`, `errors`. CI MUST fail if a second `class ServiceResult` definition is detected.
rule.rationale: LLMs invent slightly different `ServiceResult` shapes per file; divergent shapes force controllers to handle multiple cases.

rule.statement: Every Service Object MUST expose a `call` instance method (or `.call` class method) returning the shared `ServiceResult`. Constructor accepts `params:` and `current_user:` keyword args.
rule.rationale: Consistent interface makes every service discoverable + testable the same way; namespaced services (`Users::CreateService`) keep the directory navigable.

rule.statement: Mail, webhooks, search-index updates MUST fire from `after_commit` callbacks, an outbox, or chained Sidekiq jobs. `deliver_later` / external HTTP inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` is forbidden.
rule.rationale: `deliver_later` inside a transaction enqueues before commit; rollback leaves the worker running against a non-existent record.

rule.statement: Controllers MUST call `params.require(:resource).permit(:f1, :f2)` in a private `<resource>_params` method and pass its result to the service. Passing `params[:resource]` raw — to a service or to `create` / `update` — is forbidden, and services MUST NOT touch `params` or HTTP globals.
rule.rationale: Strong Parameters enforce an allowlist at the HTTP boundary; an unfiltered params hash lets a client set `is_admin` and reintroduces mass assignment wherever it lands.

rule.statement: Sidekiq jobs MUST accept primitives (IDs, strings, hashes of primitives). ActiveRecord objects MUST NOT be passed as arguments. Jobs declare `sidekiq_options retry: N, dead: true` + a backoff strategy.
rule.rationale: AR objects serialise as YAML and load a stale row on dequeue; passing IDs ensures the worker fetches latest state.

rule.statement: Migrations containing `remove_column`, `rename_column`, `change_column_default(...)` MUST require explicit human approval before `db:migrate` in any shared environment. CI MUST flag destructive migrations in the PR description.
rule.rationale: Irreversible migrations cannot be rolled back; agents generate destructive migrations without verifying column data.

section.title: Framework fundamentals (conventions)
section.p: The rules above decide how business logic is arranged; these four decide how the Rails app itself is shaped. Rails is opinionated, and fighting the convention costs months — routing, secrets, shared model logic and callbacks each have one idiomatic home.

rule.statement: Routes MUST be declared with `resources :name` (or `resource` for a singular resource), using `member` / `collection` blocks for the non-CRUD verbs and `shallow: true` for nesting. Ad-hoc `get '/path' => 'controller#action'` entries are limited to genuinely non-CRUD endpoints (health checks, webhooks) and MUST stay in single digits.
rule.rationale: Resourceful routing derives the HTTP verb mapping and the named helpers (`orders_path`, `cancel_order_path`) for free; each ad-hoc route drops out of that convention, and a routes file that is mostly ad-hoc has no consistent URL vocabulary left.

rule.statement: Production secrets MUST live in `config/credentials.yml.enc` (edited via `rails credentials:edit`, read via `Rails.application.credentials`), with the master key held outside the repo. ENV is acceptable only for non-secret configuration.
rule.rationale: Secrets in ENV surface in error-page dumps and exception-tracker context; encrypted credentials travel with the code and are decryptable only with the master key.

rule.statement: Logic shared by ≥2 models MUST live in `app/models/concerns/<Name>.rb` (and controller-shared logic in `app/controllers/concerns/`). Copy-pasting a method between models is forbidden.
rule.rationale: A concern names the shared abstraction and gives it one place to change; duplicated methods drift the moment one copy is edited.

rule.statement: Model callbacks (`before_save`, `after_create`) MUST be restricted to internal invariants — normalisation, derived fields, counters. External side effects (`deliver_later`, enqueue, publish, HTTP) MUST live in a Service Object or a job.
rule.rationale: A callback fires from every path that touches the record, so a console `touch` or a fixture load sends production email. The service is the only place where the effect is requested deliberately. Note the interaction with `after-commit-for-side-effects`: an `after_*_commit` hook that only enqueues an already-decided job is the exception this rule allows.
